description.en: Understand how many machines sharing one wire or one patch of air agree on who sends first and what to do after a collision, then see these methods strung together in a real case: Ethernet.
description.zh: 看懂很多台机器共用一条线或一片空气时，怎样约定谁先发、撞了怎么办，再用以太网把这些办法串成一个真实的案例。

description.en: Thinking the busier the line, the better the value. In fact only one frame fits at a time, and frames sent together ruin each other; when it gets busy the line is being wrecked by collisions, not filled up.
description.zh: 以为线越忙越划算。其实同一时刻只容得下一个帧，同时发会互相毁掉，忙起来是被撞坏而不是被用满。

description.en: Thinking contention protocols are always worse than collision-free ones. In fact at low load they hardly wait and have lower delay, while collision-free protocols wait for nothing at low load.
description.zh: 以为竞争协议总比无冲突协议差。其实低负载时它几乎不用等，延迟更小；无冲突协议在低负载时反而要白等。

description.en: Thinking “listen before sending” means no collisions. In fact signals take time to travel, so when you hear the line is idle someone else's frame may still be on the way; and several stations waiting for the line to go idle will all pounce at once.
description.zh: 以为「先听再发」就不会冲突。其实信号传过去要时间，听到线空时别人的帧可能还在路上；几个站同时等线空，还会一起扑上去。

description.en: Mixing up hidden and exposed terminals. A hidden terminal should have waited and did not (so frames collide); an exposed terminal should not have waited but did (concurrency wasted).
description.zh: 把隐藏终端和暴露终端搞反。隐藏终端是该等没等（结果撞坏），暴露终端是不该等却等了（白白浪费并发）。

description.en: Thinking any station that hears someone's RTS must wait until the data is done. In fact a station that hears the RTS but not the CTS is far from the receiver and can send to someone else.
description.zh: 以为听到别人 RTS 的站一律要等到数据发完。其实只听到 RTS、没听到 CTS 的站离接收者很远，可以发给别人。

description.en: Thinking two senders that cannot hear each other will not collide. In fact the collision happens at the receiver: as long as both signals reach the same receiver, they pile up and are ruined there.
description.zh: 以为两个发送者互相听不到，就不会撞。其实冲突发生在接收者那里：只要两路信号都传得到同一个接收者，就会在那里叠坏。

description.en: Thinking one more or one fewer station contending in the same slot makes little difference. In fact with one station the success rate is 1.0, and it falls fastest as the number goes from 1 to 4, so the number of contending stations should be kept very small.
description.zh: 以为同一个时隙里竞争的站多一个少一个差别不大。其实一个站时成功率是 1.0，站数从 1 到 4 降得最快，所以要把竞争的站数压到很少。

description.en: Thinking the minimum frame size is there to make up enough check bits or to save bandwidth. In fact it is so that the sender is still transmitting when the noise from a collision comes back, so it knows there was a collision.
description.zh: 以为最小帧长是为了凑够校验位或省带宽。其实是为了让发送者在冲突的噪声传回来时还在发送，才知道撞了。

description.en: Miscounting the backoff range by one. After i collisions, pick from 0 to 2^i−1, which is 2^i numbers: after 3 collisions that is 0 to 7, 8 numbers.
description.zh: 把退避范围数错一位。撞了 i 次，是在 0 到 2^i−1 里挑，共 2^i 个数：撞 3 次是 0 到 7，共 8 个数。

description.en: Thinking a MAC address and an IP address are the same thing. A MAC address is a flat factory-assigned number that works within one LAN; an IP address is hierarchical and works for delivery across networks.
description.zh: 以为 MAC 地址和 IP 地址是一回事。MAC 是平的出厂编号，管同一个局域网；IP 有层次，管跨网络送达。

description.en: Thinking the first 24 bits of a MAC address say where the network card is. In fact they only say who the vendor is; one vendor's cards are sold all over the world.
description.zh: 以为 MAC 地址前 24 位能说明网卡在哪里。其实它只说明厂商是谁，同一个厂商的网卡卖到世界各地。

description.en: Thinking each port on a switch still has to fight for the line with CSMA/CD. In fact on a full-duplex line each port has only one device, and nobody competes with it.
description.zh: 以为交换机的每个端口上还要靠 CSMA/CD 抢线。其实全双工线路上每个端口只有一台设备，没有人和它抢。

title.en: Speak whenever you like: does it work?

prompt.en: 40 machines are connected to one wire, with no agreement at all: whoever has data just sends it. Each machine has more and more data to send, and the wire gets busier and busier. What happens?
prompt.zh: 一条线上接了 40 台机器，没有任何约定：谁有数据谁就直接发。每台机器要发的数据越来越多，线越来越忙，会怎样？

label.en: The busier the better: the wire is used more and more fully, with almost no waste.
label.zh: 越忙越好，线被用得越来越满，几乎没有浪费。

feedback.en: Only one frame fits on the wire at a time. Two frames piled together are both ruined; when it gets busy the wire is not being filled up, it is being wrecked by collisions.
feedback.zh: 线上同一时刻只容得下一个帧。两个帧叠在一起就都坏了，忙起来不是被用满，而是被撞坏。

label.en: Collisions multiply, most of the wire's time goes on ruined frames and resends, and less actually gets delivered.
label.zh: 冲突越来越多，线的大部分时间花在撞坏的帧和重发上，真正送达的反而变少。

label.en: Collisions are only an occasional small matter; one resend fixes it and efficiency is hardly affected.
label.zh: 冲突只是偶尔的小事，重发一次就好，对效率几乎没影响。

feedback.en: Resent frames collide with other people's too. Once load is high, resending itself creates new collisions, so it is not a small matter.
feedback.zh: 重发的帧也会和别人的撞。负载一高，重发本身就制造新的冲突，不是小事。

label.en: The machines will line up by themselves, so there will be no collisions.
label.zh: 机器会自己排成队，所以不会有冲突。

feedback.en: With no agreement there is no queue: nobody knows when anyone else wants to send. What queueing needs is precisely an agreement.
feedback.zh: 没有约定就没有队：谁也不知道别人什么时候想发。排队需要的恰恰是约定。

explain.en: A shared wire holds only one frame at a time. Sending whenever you like is fine at low load; once load is high, frames ruin each other, resends are ruined again, and throughput actually falls. What the next few pages solve is this: how to agree so that everyone shares quickly and fairly.
explain.zh: 一条共用的线同一时刻只容得下一个帧。想发就发，负载低时还行；负载一高，帧互相撞坏，重发又撞坏，吞吐量反而下降。接下来几页要解决的就是：怎样约定，让大家共用得又快又公平。

text.en: The data link layer in the previous lesson was about making things reliable between two neighbouring machines. But “neighbouring” is not always one-to-one: in a dorm your laptop and your roommate's phone share the same patch of air (Wi-Fi), and early office networks had dozens of computers hanging on one wire.
text.zh: 上一课的数据链路层讲的是相邻两台机器之间怎样可靠。可「相邻」不一定是一对一：宿舍里你的笔记本和室友的手机共用同一片空气（Wi-Fi），早期的办公室网络是几十台电脑挂在同一根线上。

text.en: When two people talk at once, nobody can be heard. In networks this is called a **collision**: two frames pile up on one channel at the same moment, and both are ruined. The part of the data link layer devoted to “who may send, and when” is called the **medium access control (MAC) sublayer**.
text.zh: 两个人同时说话，谁都听不清。网络里把这叫**冲突** (collision)：两个帧同一时刻叠在同一条信道上，都坏了。数据链路层里专管「谁什么时候可以发」的那一部分，叫**介质访问控制子层** (MAC sublayer, medium access control)。

text.en: A good agreement has to do two things: be **efficient** (the channel shouldn't sit idle for nothing, nor be burned on collisions) and **fair** (every machine gets a chance). The methods fall into three families, compared with a classroom:
text.zh: 一个好的约定要做到两件事：**高效**（信道别白白空着，也别耗在冲突上）和**公平**（每台机器都有机会）。办法分三大类，用教室来比：

items.en: **Contention**: there is no teacher; you speak when you want, stop if you collide, and wait a while before speaking again.
items.zh: **竞争** (contention)：没有老师，想说就开口，撞了就停下，等一会儿再说。

items.en: **Collision-free**: the teacher calls roll by seat number; you speak only when your turn comes, so there are no collisions.
items.zh: **无冲突** (collision-free)：老师按座位号点名，轮到你才说，不会撞。

items.en: **Limited contention**: split into small groups, and fight to speak only within the group.
items.zh: **受限竞争** (limited contention)：分成小组，只在组里抢着说。

text.en: The first two each have their own faults. Look at them first, then at how to compromise.
text.zh: 前两类各有各的毛病。先看它们，再看怎样折中。

text.en: The simplest agreement is no agreement. Contention protocols start from here and add rules step by step:
text.zh: 最简单的约定是没有约定。竞争类协议从这里出发，一步步加规矩：

rows.en: Send as soon as you have a frame; if no acknowledgement arrives, wait a random time and send again
rows.zh: 有帧就立刻发；收不到确认，就等一个随机时间再发

rows.en: Simple; but anyone who starts sending within one frame time before or after you collides with you
rows.zh: 简单；但别人在你发的前后各一个帧长的时间里开始发，都会撞上你

rows.en: Time is cut into slots one frame long, and sending is allowed only at the start of a slot
rows.zh: 时间切成一帧长的时隙，只能在时隙开头发

rows.en: The window for collisions is halved
rows.zh: 撞车的时间窗缩短一半

rows.en: Listen to see whether anyone is sending before you send
rows.zh: 发之前先听线上有没有人在发

rows.en: Hearing idle does not mean nobody is sending: someone may already be sending and the signal has not reached me yet
rows.zh: 听到空闲，不等于没有人在发：有人可能已经在发，只是信号还没传到我这里

rows.en: If the line is busy, keep listening and send the moment it goes idle (the probability of sending is 1)
rows.zh: 线忙就一直听，一空闲马上发（发的概率是 1）

rows.en: When several stations are waiting they pounce together and certainly collide
rows.zh: 几个站都在等时，会同时扑上去，必撞

rows.en: If the line is busy, back off a random time first, then listen again
rows.zh: 线忙就先退一个随机时间，再来听

rows.en: They do not pounce together; but the line may have been idle for a while with you still waiting, so delay grows
rows.zh: 不会同时扑上去；但线早空了，自己还在等，延迟变大

rows.en: When idle, send with probability p, and with probability 1−p wait for the next slot and look again
rows.zh: 一空闲，以概率 p 发，以 1−p 等到下一个时隙再看

rows.en: A compromise between the two above
Keep listening while sending, and stop at once on finding a collision
rows.zh: 发的同时继续听，发现撞了立刻停

rows.en: A ruined frame wastes time only until the collision is noticed, not the whole frame
rows.zh: 撞坏的帧只浪费到发现为止，不必发完

body.en: At low load, send when you want and hardly wait, so delay is very small. At high load, everyone collides together, and a great deal of time is wasted on collisions and resends. This temperament of contention protocols will be used again and again later.
body.zh: 负载低时，想发就发，几乎不用等，延迟很小。负载高时，大家一起撞，大量时间浪费在冲突和重发上。竞争类的这个脾气，后面要反复用到。

body.en: Even at its best, pure ALOHA spends only about 18% of the time carrying useful frames ($1/(2e)$); slotted ALOHA about 37% ($1/e$). These two numbers are not in the slides; what the exam wants is the conclusion that “contention protocols waste a lot at high load”.
body.zh: 纯 ALOHA 最好时，也只有约 18% 的时间在送有用的帧 ($1/(2e)$)；时隙 ALOHA 约 37% ($1/e$)。这两个数课件里没有；考试要的是「高负载下竞争协议浪费大」这个结论。

text.en: The trouble with contention is that frames collide. So simply don't let them: register first, then take turns in order.
text.zh: 竞争的毛病是会撞。那就干脆不让它撞：先登记，再按顺序轮流发。

text.en: Bit map
text.zh: 位图 (bit map)

text.en: Say there are 8 machines, numbered 0 to 7. Each round begins with 8 very short registration slots: in slot i only machine i may speak, putting a 1 if it has a frame to send and leaving 0 if not. After registration everyone knows who wants to send, and then they send one by one in numbered order.
text.zh: 设有 8 台机器，编号 0 到 7。每一轮先有 8 个很短的登记时隙：第 i 格只有 i 号机器可以说话，有帧要发就填 1，没有就留 0。登记完，人人都知道谁要发，然后按编号顺序一个一个发。

alt.en: The 8 registration slots read 0 1 0 1 0 0 1 0, after which machines 1, 3 and 6 send their frames in turn

caption.en: Stations 1, 3 and 6 want to send: after registration, they take turns in numbered order.
caption.zh: 1、3、6 号想发：登记之后，按编号顺序轮流发。

text.en: No collisions, and nobody is starved. The price is the registration itself: whether or not anyone has something to send, each round must first run through all 8 slots. At low load, a machine that has just missed its own slot has to wait a whole round; at high load each frame carries only one bit of registration, so the overhead is small.
text.zh: 没有冲突，也没有人会被饿死。代价是登记本身：不管有没有人要发，每轮都要先走完 8 格。负载低时，一台机器刚错过自己的那一格，就要等一整轮；负载高时，每个帧只摊到一位登记，开销很小。

text.en: Binary countdown
text.zh: 二进制倒计数 (binary countdown)

text.en: Use the stations' binary addresses in place of registration. Stations that want to send put their address bits on the line one at a time, starting from the highest bit; for a given bit position, if anyone puts a 1 the result on the line is 1 (equivalent to taking the “OR”). A station that put a 0 but sees a 1 on the line knows that a station with a larger address also wants to send, and drops out.
text.zh: 用站的二进制地址来代替登记。想发的站从最高位开始，把自己地址的每一位依次放到线上；线上同一位只要有人放 1，结果就是 1（相当于取「或」）。某个站放的是 0，却看到线上是 1，就知道有地址更大的站也要发，自己退出。

text.en: Example: 8 machines, 3-bit addresses, and stations 010, 100 and 101 want to send.
text.zh: 例子：8 台机器，3 位地址，010、100、101 三个站想发。

text.en: 101 is left; it wins and sends first. The overhead per frame is only the number of address bits: for 8 machines that is $\log_2 8 = 3$ bits. The price is that stations with large addresses always have the advantage.
text.zh: 剩下 101，它赢，先发。每个帧的开销只是地址的位数：8 台机器是 $\log_2 8 = 3$ 位。代价是地址大的站总占便宜。

prompt.en: A lab's local network: in the early morning only 2 machines occasionally send a little data; in the evening 40 machines always have data to send. For the early morning and the evening, is each better suited to a contention protocol or a collision-free protocol? Give a one-sentence reason for each.
prompt.zh: 一间实验室的局域网：凌晨只有 2 台机器偶尔发一点数据；晚上 40 台机器一直都有数据要发。凌晨和晚上，各更适合竞争协议还是无冲突协议？各用一句话说理由。

key_points.en: In the evening (high load) a collision-free protocol is better suited
key_points.zh: 晚上（高负载）更适合无冲突协议

key_points.en: Reason: contention protocols then collide often and time goes on ruined frames and resends; a collision-free protocol lets each station take turns on the channel, with no collisions
key_points.zh: 理由：竞争协议此时冲突频繁，时间耗在撞坏的帧和重发上；无冲突协议让每个站轮流用信道，不撞

key_points.en: In the early morning (low load) a contention protocol is better suited
key_points.zh: 凌晨（低负载）更适合竞争协议

key_points.en: Reason: send when you want, hardly any waiting, small delay; a collision-free protocol has to register first or wait its turn, needlessly adding delay
key_points.zh: 理由：想发就发，几乎不用等，延迟小；无冲突协议要先登记或等轮到自己，白白增加延迟

model_answer.en: In the evening the load is high, so use a collision-free protocol: a contention protocol would collide constantly, with all the time wasted on collisions and resends, while a collision-free protocol has every station send in turn and the channel is used fully. In the early morning the load is low, so use a contention protocol: send when you want, with hardly any waiting and small delay; a collision-free protocol has to register first or wait its turn, so it waits for nothing.
model_answer.zh: 晚上负载高，用无冲突协议：竞争协议会撞个不停，时间都浪费在冲突和重发上，而无冲突协议让每个站按顺序轮流发，信道用得满。凌晨负载低，用竞争协议：想发就发，几乎不用等，延迟小；无冲突协议要先登记或等轮到自己，反而白等。

hints.en: Think: when do frames collide? When does a machine want to send and yet have to wait for others?
hints.zh: 想一想：什么时候会撞？什么时候一台机器想发，却还要等别人？

explain.en: At high load, contention protocols collide a lot and waste a lot, while collision-free protocols take turns in order and are more efficient; this is the conclusion the official sample question wants. At low load it is the other way round: contention protocols have no registration or queueing overhead, so delay is small. Each kind has a load it is good at, which is why a compromise is needed.
explain.zh: 高负载时，竞争协议冲突多、浪费大，无冲突协议按顺序轮流，更高效，这就是官方样题要的结论。低负载时反过来：竞争协议没有登记和排队的开销，延迟小。两类各有擅长的负载，所以才需要折中。

title.en: With more stations, where does the success rate fall to
title.zh: 站多了，成功率掉到哪里

intro.en: The idea: don't let too many stations fight for one slot. Split the stations into groups and let only one group contend in each slot. All stations in one group is pure contention; one station per group is taking turns. Adjust the group size between the two ends, and with fewer contenders there are fewer collisions. Why does “fewer” matter so much? First work out the success probability. Suppose $k$ stations in a slot want to send, each trying with the same probability $p$. Only “exactly one station sends” counts as success, and this is the probability $P$ to be computed.
intro.zh: 想法是：别让太多站同时抢一个时隙。把站分成组，每个时隙只让一组去抢。全体站放一组，就是纯竞争；每组只放一个站，就是轮流。组的大小在这两头之间调，抢的人少了，撞得就少。为什么「少」这么要紧？先算成功概率。设某个时隙里有 $k$ 个站想发，每个站都以同样的概率 $p$ 去试。只有「恰好一个站发」才算成功，要算的就是这个概率 $P$。

why.en: First pick the station that sends ($k$ ways to choose), which sends with probability $p$; the other $k-1$ all hold back, each with probability $1-p$.
why.zh: 先选出那个发的站（$k$ 种选法），它发的概率是 $p$；其余 $k-1$ 个都不发，各是 $1-p$。

why.en: $P$ is largest at $p=1/k$: on average exactly one station is trying in each slot. After substitution $k\cdot\tfrac1k=1$. This is the best case contention can achieve.
why.zh: $p=1/k$ 时 $P$ 最大：平均每个时隙恰好一个站在试。代入后 $k\cdot\tfrac1k=1$。这是竞争能做到的最好情形。

why.en: Substituting one by one: $P(3)=(2/3)^2$, $P(5)=(4/5)^4$. With one station there is no collision and the success rate is 100%; with two or three stations it drops to about 0.4.
With still more stations it only creeps towards $1/e$. This is the curve in the slides: a steep fall at first, then flat at around 0.4.
why.zh: 站再多，也只是缓缓逼近 $1/e$。这就是课件那条曲线：先陡降，后持平在 0.4 附近。

lines.tex: \text{一次成功平均要试 } \dfrac{1}{1/e} = e \approx 2.7 \text{ 个时隙}

why.en: The probability of success in each slot is $1/e$, so on average $e$ slots are needed for one success. When we work out Ethernet's efficiency later, this $e$ will appear again.
why.zh: 每个时隙成功的概率是 $1/e$，平均要试 $e$ 个时隙才成功一次。后面算以太网的效率时，这个 $e$ 会再出现。

outro.en: How to read it: with one station success is certain; once there are more, the success rate settles below 0.4 and cannot be rescued however many more there are. So the number of stations contending in each slot should be kept on the leftmost, highest stretch of the curve. At low load groups can be larger, almost like contention where you send when you want; at high load groups shrink very small, almost like collision-free taking of turns. That is the answer to the question at the start of the slides, “contention model plus collision-free model?”: squeeze down the waste at both ends, the idle slots and the slots spent on contending.
outro.zh: 读法：一个站时稳稳成功，站一多，成功率就停在 0.4 以下，再多也救不回来。所以要把每个时隙里竞争的站数压在曲线最靠左、最高的那一段。负载低时，组可以大一些，几乎像竞争那样想发就发；负载高时，组缩得很小，几乎像无冲突那样轮流。课件开头那句「竞争模型加无冲突模型？」的答案就是这样：两头的浪费，空闲的时隙和用来竞争的时隙，都压下来。

prompt.en: In a slot only one group of stations contends. $k$ stations in the group want to send right now, each trying with the optimal probability $1/k$, so the success probability is $(1-1/k)^{k-1}$. Which of the four values of $k$ below makes this slot's success probability fall below 0.4?
prompt.zh: 一个时隙里只让一组站竞争，组内此刻想发的站有 $k$ 个，每个站都以最优概率 $1/k$ 去试，成功概率是 $(1-1/k)^{k-1}$。下面四个 $k$，哪一个会让这个时隙的成功概率掉到 0.4 以下？

feedback.en: $P(2)=(1/2)^1=0.50$: not only has it not fallen below 0.4, it is the highest of these. The fewer the stations, the higher the success rate.
feedback.zh: $P(2)=(1/2)^1=0.50$，不但没掉到 0.4 以下，还是这几个里最高的。站越少，成功率越高。

feedback.en: $P(3)=(2/3)^2\approx0.44$, still above 0.4. The success rate falls steadily as stations are added, and at three stations it has not fallen much yet.
feedback.zh: $P(3)=(2/3)^2\approx0.44$，仍在 0.4 以上。成功率是随站数一路往下掉的，三个站时还没掉多少。

feedback.en: $P(5)=(4/5)^4\approx0.41$, only just above 0.4. It takes more stations to fall below it.
feedback.zh: $P(5)=(4/5)^4\approx0.41$，刚好还在 0.4 以上。要站更多，才会掉到它下面。

hints.en: Substitute $k$ into $(1-1/k)^{k-1}$ and work it out: which of $P(5)$ and $P(10)$ falls below 0.4 first?

explain.en: $P(2)=0.50$, $P(3)\approx0.44$, $P(5)\approx0.41$, $P(10)\approx0.39$. The curve falls fastest over the first few stations and then stays roughly flat below 0.4. So the point of grouping is to keep the number actually contending in each slot to no more than a few, so the success probability stays on the highest stretch of the curve.
explain.zh: $P(2)=0.50$，$P(3)\approx0.44$，$P(5)\approx0.41$，$P(10)\approx0.39$。曲线前几站降得最快，之后基本持平在 0.4 以下。所以分组的用处，是让每个时隙里真正在抢的站不超过几个，成功概率就留在曲线最高的那一段。

title.en: Adaptive tree walk: on a collision, split in half
title.zh: 自适应树遍历：冲突就对半分

text.en: One concrete way to do grouping: put the 8 stations A to H on the leaves of a binary tree. Each internal node stands for the group of stations below it: node 1 is the root (all of A–H), node 2 is A–D, node 3 is E–H, node 4 is A, B, and so on.
text.zh: 分组的一种具体做法：把 8 个站 A 到 H 放在一棵二叉树的叶子上。每个内部结点代表它下面的一组站：1 号是根（全体 A–H），2 号是 A–D，3 号是 E–H，4 号是 A、B，依此类推。

alt.en: Binary tree: node 1 is the root, nodes 2 and 3 are on the next level, nodes 4 to 7 on the level after, and the leaves are stations A to H
alt.zh: 二叉树：1 号是根，2、3 号在下一层，4 到 7 号再下一层，叶子是站 A 到 H

caption.en: Circles are groups, squares are stations.

text.en: Each slot corresponds to one node in the tree: in that slot, the stations below that node that want to send may send. There are only three outcomes:
text.zh: 每个时隙对应树上的一个结点：这个时隙里，该结点下面想发的站可以发。结果只有三种：

items.en: Nobody wants to send: the slot is idle, and the whole subtree need not be looked at again.
items.zh: 没人想发：这个时隙空闲，整棵子树不用再看。

items.en: Exactly one wants to send: success, and it sends its frame.
items.zh: 恰好一人想发：成功，它发完。

items.en: Two or more want to send: a collision. Next test its left and right child nodes, splitting the colliding group in half.
items.zh: 两人以上想发：冲突。接着去测它的左、右两个子结点，把冲突的这一组对半分开。

text.en: The order is **depth first**: a colliding node is explored down the left side all the way, and only then do we come back to the right. Nodes with no collision are not split further, so splitting continues only in groups where “several stations want to send”.
text.zh: 顺序是**深度优先** (depth first search)：冲突的结点先钻到左边一路查完，再回头查右边。没有冲突的结点不会再往下分，所以只在「有多个站想发」的组里继续分。

body.en: At low load, often only one or two stations want to send, and the first slot at node 1 already succeeds, wasting nothing.
body.zh: 负载低时，常常只有一两个站想发，1 号结点的第一个时隙就成功了，一点也不浪费。

text.en: Take the slides' two examples and match each slot to a node in the tree.
text.zh: 把课件的两个例子，每个时隙对到树上的结点来看。

text.en: Example 1: D and G want to send
text.zh: 例 1：D、G 想发

head.en: Stations in it that want to send

text.en: Example 2: B, D and G want to send
text.zh: 例 2：B、D、G 想发

head.en: Stations in it that want to send

text.en: Note that after the collision in slot 2, we go down under node 2 first (nodes 4 and 5), and only come back to node 3 after finishing. This is depth first.
text.zh: 注意第 2 个时隙冲突之后，先钻进 2 号下面（4 号、5 号），查完了才回到 3 号。这就是深度优先。

text.en: Why it is called “adaptive”
text.zh: 为什么叫「自适应」

text.en: The more stations want to send, the more certainly the levels near the root collide, which is pure waste. If all 8 stations want to send, starting at the root means testing all 15 nodes: 7 collisions plus 8 successes, 15 slots in all. If we start directly at level 2 (nodes 4 to 7), it takes only 4 collisions plus 8 successes, 12 slots.
text.zh: 想发的站越多，靠近根的那几层越是必然冲突，纯属浪费。8 个站全想发，从根开始要把 15 个结点全查一遍：7 次冲突加 8 次成功，共 15 个时隙。如果直接从第 2 层（4 到 7 号）开始，只要 4 次冲突加 8 次成功，12 个时隙。

text.en: So **at low load start from the root, at high load start from a deeper level**, adjusting itself to the load; this is what “adaptive” means. The worst case is testing every node: 8 stations take 15 slots.
text.zh: 所以**负载低就从根开始，负载高就从更深的一层开始**，随负载自己调整，这就是「自适应」(adaptive)。最坏的情况是每个结点都查一遍：8 个站要 15 个时隙。

body.en: Which level is the best place to start? Roughly, so that on average there is 1 station wanting to send under each node: when $q$ stations want to send, start at level $\log_2 q$. The slides do not ask you to compute this, only to be able to say “at high load, start from a deep level”.
body.zh: 起点选在哪一层最好？大致让每个结点下平均有 1 个想发的站：$q$ 个站想发时，从第 $\log_2 q$ 层开始。课件不要求算这个，只要能说出「高负载从深层开始」。

prompt.en: The same tree: node 1 is the root, node 2 is A–D, node 3 is E–H, node 4 is A, B, node 5 is C, D, node 6 is E, F, node 7 is G, H. Now stations A, B and E want to send. Starting from the root, how many slots in all until everything has been sent? (Idle slots count too.)
prompt.zh: 还是那棵树：1 号是根，2 号是 A–D，3 号是 E–H，4 号是 A、B，5 号是 C、D，6 号是 E、F，7 号是 G、H。现在 A、B、E 三个站想发，从根开始，一共要几个时隙才全部发完？（空闲的时隙也算。）

hints.en: List slot by slot: the node number, the stations in it that want to send, and whether it is a collision, a success or idle.
hints.zh: 逐个时隙列出来：结点号、里面想发的站、冲突还是成功还是空闲。

hints.en: Depth first: after the collision at node 2, test node 4 first, then node 5, and only then come back to node 3.
hints.zh: 深度优先：2 号冲突后先查 4 号，再查 5 号，最后才回到 3 号。

explain.en: Slot 1: node 1, A, B, E collide. Slot 2: node 2 (A–D), A and B collide. Slot 3: node 4 (A, B), still a collision. Slot 4: A succeeds. Slot 5: B succeeds. Slot 6: node 5 (C, D), nobody wants to send, idle. Slot 7: node 3 (E–H), only E, success. 7 in all.
explain.zh: 时隙 1：1 号，A、B、E 冲突。时隙 2：2 号（A–D），A、B 冲突。时隙 3：4 号（A、B），仍然冲突。时隙 4：A 成功。时隙 5：B 成功。时隙 6：5 号（C、D），没人想发，空闲。时隙 7：3 号（E–H），只有 E，成功。共 7 个。

title.en: The trouble with wireless: the one who listens and the one who gets hit are not the same
title.zh: 无线的麻烦：听的人和被撞的人不是同一个

text.en: “Listen before sending” works well in the wired world: the wire isn't long, and whoever is sending, everyone hears. Wireless is different: each machine's signal carries only a limited distance, and the stations' ranges only partly overlap.
text.zh: 「先听再发」在有线世界里很好用：线不长，谁在发，大家都听得到。无线不一样：每台机器的信号只传得到有限的距离，各站的范围只是互相重叠一部分。

text.en: Carrier sensing happens at the **sender**'s end: quiet here only means it is quiet here. But collisions happen at the **receiver**'s end: whether someone else is sending near the receiver, I cannot hear.
text.zh: 载波侦听 (carrier sensing) 发生在**发送者**这一端：我这里安静，只说明我这里安静。可冲突发生在**接收者**那一端：接收者那里有没有别人在发，我听不到。

alt.en: The signal ranges of A and C overlap in one area, and D is in the overlap; B is far away, outside both ranges
alt.zh: A 和 C 的信号范围有一块重叠，D 在重叠区里；B 在远处，不在任何一个范围内

caption.en: Dashed circles are the range each station's signal can reach.
caption.zh: 虚线圈是各站信号能到的范围。

text.en: The A, D, C, B circle diagram in the slides is about this: the ranges of A and C overlap, D stands in the overlap and hears both A and C. If A and C send at the same time, the two signals pile up at D and nothing can be received. B is far away and unaffected.
text.zh: 课件里那张 A、D、C、B 的圆圈图说的就是这件事：A 和 C 的范围有一块重叠，D 站在重叠区里，同时听到 A 和 C。A、C 同时发，D 那里两路信号叠在一起，什么也收不到。B 离得很远，不受影响。

text.en: So what wireless needs to detect is transmission **around the receiver**; the sender listening by itself is not enough. This produces two opposite kinds of trouble, seen on the next page.
text.zh: 所以无线要检测的是**接收方周围**的传输，光靠发送者自己听不够。由此冒出两种相反的毛病，下一页看。

body.en: The wireless protocols the slides name are 802.11 (today's Wi-Fi) and MACAW. The Wi-Fi in your dorm follows 802.11.
body.zh: 课件点名的无线协议是 802.11（今天的 Wi-Fi）和 MACAW。你宿舍里的 Wi-Fi 遵守的就是 802.11。

text.en: Hidden terminal: should have waited and didn't
text.zh: 隐藏终端 (hidden terminal)：该等的没等

text.en: A row of four stations A, B, C, D, each hearing only its neighbours. A and C both want to send to B. A and C are far apart and cannot hear each other: A hears the line quiet and sends, C also hears it quiet and sends, and the two signals collide at B. A and C are “hidden” from each other. This is **should have waited and didn't**: the collision is a waste and has to be avoided.
text.zh: 一排四个站 A、B、C、D，每个站只听得到相邻的站。A 和 C 都想发给 B。A 与 C 隔得远，彼此听不到：A 听到线上安静就发，C 也听到安静就发，两路信号在 B 那里撞坏。A 和 C 对彼此是「隐藏」的。这是**该等没等**：撞坏了就浪费，要避免。

alt.en: A and C both send to B. A's range ends at B, C's range covers B and D, and A and C are outside each other's range
alt.zh: A 和 C 都向 B 发送。A 的范围到 B 为止，C 的范围到 B 和 D，A 与 C 互相在对方范围之外

caption.en: A and C cannot hear each other and send to B at the same time: they collide at B.
caption.zh: A、C 互相听不到，同时发给 B：在 B 处撞坏。

text.en: Exposed terminal: shouldn't have waited but did
text.zh: 暴露终端 (exposed terminal)：不该等却等了

text.en: The same row of stations, this time B sends to A and C sends to D. B and C can hear each other: C hears B sending and, following “listen before sending”, obediently waits. But B's signal cannot reach D and C's signal cannot reach A, so the two could have gone on at the same time without interfering. C waited for nothing. This is **shouldn't have waited but did**: concurrency wasted. This kind of sending at the same time is a good thing and raises performance.
text.zh: 同一排站，这次是 B 发给 A，C 发给 D。B 和 C 听得到彼此：C 听到 B 在发，按「先听再发」就乖乖等着。可是 B 的信号到不了 D，C 的信号也到不了 A，两件事本来能同时进行，互不干扰。C 白白等了。这是**不该等却等了**：浪费了并发。这种同时发的情形是好事，能提高性能。

alt.en: B sends to A and C sends to D. B and C are within each other's range, but A is only in B's range and D only in C's range
alt.zh: B 发给 A，C 发给 D。B 和 C 在彼此范围内，但 A 只在 B 的范围内，D 只在 C 的范围内

caption.en: B and C can hear each other, but each sends to its own receiver, so they could in fact send at the same time.
caption.zh: B、C 听得到彼此，但各发各的接收者，其实可以同时发。

rows.en: The two senders cannot hear each other
rows.zh: 两个发送者互相听不到

rows.en: The two senders can hear each other
rows.zh: 两个发送者互相听得到

rows.en: The same receiver (A and C both send to B)
rows.zh: 同一个接收者（A、C 都发给 B）

rows.en: Different receivers (B sends to A, C sends to D)
rows.zh: 不同的接收者（B 发给 A，C 发给 D）

rows.en: Hears quiet and sends, and they collide
Hears someone sending and waits, though they would not collide
rows.zh: 听到有人发就等，其实不会撞

rows.en: Frames are ruined, efficiency is lost, must be avoided
rows.zh: 撞坏帧，损失效率，要避免

rows.en: Concurrency wasted; this concurrency is a good thing
rows.zh: 浪费并发；这种并发是好事

body.en: Both are ways carrier sensing fails in wireless: a hidden terminal should have waited and didn't, so there is a collision; an exposed terminal shouldn't have waited but did, so things are slow.
body.zh: 两者都是载波侦听在无线里失灵的表现：隐藏终端是该等没等，结果撞；暴露终端是不该等却等了，结果慢。

text.en: The trouble is at the receiver, so let the receiver speak. Before sending the long data frame, first use two very short control frames to settle things:
text.zh: 问题出在接收者那里，就让接收者开口。发长长的数据帧之前，先用两个很短的控制帧问清楚：

items.en: **RTS** (Request-to-Send): A first sends a short frame to B: “I want to send to you, this much data”.
items.zh: **RTS** (Request-to-Send)：A 先发一个短帧给 B：「我要给你发，数据这么长」。

items.en: **CTS** (Clear-to-Send): B replies with a short frame: “OK, I'm ready”, again carrying the data length.
items.zh: **CTS** (Clear-to-Send)：B 回一个短帧：「可以，我准备好了」，同样带着数据长度。

items.en: Only when A hears the CTS does it send the data frame.
items.zh: A 听到 CTS，才发数据帧。

text.en: The key is what bystanders do: whose short frame you hear decides whether you should send.
text.zh: 关键在旁人怎么办：听到谁的短帧，决定你该不该发。

alt.en: Left: A sends an RTS whose range covers C, B and E; right: B replies with a CTS whose range covers A, D and E. Stations that hear it are marked yellow
alt.zh: 左图：A 发 RTS，范围覆盖 C、B、E；右图：B 回 CTS，范围覆盖 A、D、E。听到的站标成黄色

caption.en: Yellow stations are those that hear a short frame and must defer. C hears only the RTS, D hears only the CTS, and E hears both.
caption.zh: 黄色的站是听到短帧、要推迟的站。C 只听得到 RTS，D 只听得到 CTS，E 两个都听得到。

rows.en: Only the RTS (next to A, far from B)
rows.zh: 只听到 RTS（在 A 旁边，离 B 远）

rows.en: Waits for the CTS time; if it hears no CTS, it can send to someone else
rows.zh: 先等 CTS 的时间；没听到 CTS，就可以发给别人

rows.en: Its signal cannot reach B, so it will not ruin B's reception: it is an exposed terminal, and the concurrency is kept
rows.zh: 它的信号到不了 B，不会撞坏 B 收数据：它是暴露终端，并发被保留

rows.en: Only the CTS (next to B, far from A)
rows.zh: 只听到 CTS（在 B 旁边，离 A 远）

rows.en: Waits until the exchange is over before sending
rows.zh: 等到数据交换结束再发

rows.en: D cannot hear A, so it was originally a hidden terminal of A; the CTS tells it B is receiving and not to send near B
rows.zh: D 听不到 A，本来是 A 的隐藏终端；CTS 告诉它 B 正在收，不要在 B 旁边发

rows.en: Both RTS and CTS (between A and B)
rows.zh: RTS 和 CTS 都听到（在 A、B 之间）

rows.en: Waits until the exchange is over
Very close to B, so sending would at once ruin the reception at B
rows.zh: 离 B 很近，一发就撞坏 B 那里的接收

text.en: In this way the hidden terminal D, hearing the CTS, does not send and a collision is avoided; the exposed terminal C, hearing no CTS, can send as usual. The slides' conclusion “A can send; there are exposed terminals but no hidden terminals” says exactly this. How long must a station that hears a CTS wait? The CTS carries the data length, so it knows.
text.zh: 这样，隐藏终端 D 因为听到 CTS 而不发，避免了撞；暴露终端 C 没听到 CTS，照样可以发。课件的结论「A 能发送，有暴露终端但没有隐藏终端」说的就是这个。听到 CTS 的站要等多久？CTS 里带着数据长度，所以它知道。

text.en: The RTS can itself collide (two stations sending RTS to the same station at the same time). But an RTS is very short, so a collision costs little: the sender gets no CTS, waits a random while and resends the RTS, the same idea as ALOHA's “collide, wait a random time, send again”. Compared with letting a data frame thousands of bits long be wasted in a collision, it is far cheaper.
text.zh: RTS 自己也可能撞（两个站同时向同一个站发 RTS）。但 RTS 很短，撞了损失很小：发送者等不到 CTS，就随机等一会儿再重发 RTS，和 ALOHA 里撞了随机等一会儿再发是同一种想法。比起让几千位的数据帧白白撞坏，便宜得多。

text.en: The slides only name MACAW. It improves on MACA, broadly by adding acknowledgements to data frames and improving backoff, making wireless links more reliable. In 802.11 (Wi-Fi), RTS/CTS is also one of the optional mechanisms, used against hidden terminals. The exam only asks you to explain MACA's RTS/CTS clearly.
text.zh: 课件只点了 MACAW 的名字。它在 MACA 的基础上做了改进，大致是给数据帧加确认、改进退避，让无线链路更可靠。802.11（Wi-Fi）里，RTS/CTS 也是可选的机制之一，用来对付隐藏终端。考试只要求你能讲清 MACA 的 RTS/CTS。

title.en: The station that hears the CTS

prompt.en: Again a row of four stations P, Q, R, S, each hearing only its neighbours. This time P wants to send data to Q: P sent an RTS and Q replied with a CTS. R wants to send data to S; it cannot hear P but did hear Q's CTS. What should R do?
prompt.zh: 还是一排四个站 P、Q、R、S，每个站只听得到相邻的站。这次是 P 要给 Q 发数据：P 发了 RTS，Q 回了 CTS。R 想给 S 发数据，它听不到 P，却听到了 Q 的 CTS。R 该怎么办？

label.en: Send to S: R and P cannot hear each other, so the two signals will not collide.
label.zh: 可以发给 S：R 和 P 互相听不到，两边的信号不会撞。

feedback.en: Collisions happen at the receiver, not between the two senders. R's signal cannot reach P, but it will reach Q, where it piles up with the data P is sending and ruins it.
feedback.zh: 冲突发生在接收者那里，不在两个发送者之间。R 的信号到不了 P，却会传到 Q，在 Q 处和 P 正在发来的数据叠在一起撞坏。

label.en: Wait until it hears P's RTS and then decide.
label.zh: 等到听见 P 的 RTS 再决定。

feedback.en: R is too far from P and will never hear P's RTS; that is exactly what “hidden” means. Q's CTS is what carries the message to R on P's behalf.
feedback.zh: R 离 P 太远，永远听不到 P 的 RTS，这正是它「隐藏」的意思。Q 的 CTS 就是替 P 把消息带到 R 这里的。

label.en: Defer, and wait for Q to finish receiving: the CTS carries the data length, so wait that long before sending.
label.zh: 先推迟，等 Q 收完：CTS 里带着数据长度，等那么久再发。

label.en: Jump in first and send Q an RTS, so Q receives R's first.
label.zh: 抢先给 Q 发 RTS，让 Q 先收自己的。

feedback.en: Q is receiving P's data right now, and once R's signal piles on, P's data is ruined. However short the RTS, it should not be sent to the receiver while it is receiving someone else's data.
feedback.zh: Q 此刻正在接收 P 的数据，R 的信号一叠上去，P 的数据就撞坏了。RTS 再短，也不该在别人收数据的时候发到接收者那里。

explain.en: R is a hidden terminal of P: P and R cannot hear each other, yet both are within Q's signal range. Whoever R wants to send to, the signal will reach Q and ruin P's data at Q. With carrier sensing alone, R hears quiet and would send; with the CTS, Q has said “I am receiving” somewhere R can hear it, the data length is in it too, and R just waits that long before sending.
explain.zh: R 是 P 的隐藏终端：P 和 R 互相听不到，却都在 Q 的信号范围内。不管 R 想发给谁，信号都会传到 Q，在 Q 处撞坏 P 的数据。只靠载波侦听，R 听到的是安静，就会发；有了 CTS，Q 在 R 听得到的地方说了一声「我正在收」，数据长度也在里面，R 等那么久再发就行。

prompt.en: A row of four stations P, Q, R, S, each hearing only its neighbours. Q wants to send data to P, and first sends an RTS; P replies with a CTS. At this moment R wants to send data to S. R heard Q's RTS but did not hear P's CTS. What should R do?
prompt.zh: 一排四个站 P、Q、R、S，每个站只听得到相邻的站。Q 要给 P 发数据，先发了 RTS，P 回了 CTS。这时 R 想给 S 发数据。R 听到了 Q 的 RTS，但没听到 P 的 CTS。R 该怎么办？

label.en: It must wait until Q has finished sending, because it heard the RTS.
label.zh: 必须一直等到 Q 发完数据，因为它听到了 RTS。

feedback.en: This is what you would do with carrier sensing alone. The RTS only shows someone wants to send; what really needs protecting is the receiver P. R did not hear P's CTS, which shows it is far from P and will not ruin P's reception.
feedback.zh: 这是只靠载波侦听时的做法。RTS 只说明有人要发，真正要保护的是接收者 P；R 没听到 P 的 CTS，说明它离 P 很远，不会撞坏 P。

label.en: Send to S: not hearing a CTS shows it is far from P, so it will not ruin P's reception.
label.zh: 可以发给 S：没听到 CTS，说明它离 P 很远，不会撞坏 P 收数据。

label.en: It must wait: R and P cannot hear each other, so R is a hidden terminal.
label.zh: 必须等：R 和 P 互相听不到，所以 R 是隐藏终端。

feedback.en: A hidden terminal is when two senders send to the same receiver. Here R sends to S, its signal cannot reach P, and it will not touch P's reception at all.
feedback.zh: 隐藏终端是两个发送者发给同一个接收者。这里 R 发给 S，信号到不了 P，根本不会撞到 P 的接收。

label.en: It cannot send: a wireless channel can have only one pair of stations communicating at a time.
label.zh: 不能发：无线信道同一时间只能有一对站在通信。

feedback.en: Limited range means stations far enough apart can communicate at the same time. Keeping this concurrency is exactly where RTS/CTS beats plain carrier sensing.
feedback.zh: 范围有限，就意味着相隔够远的站可以同时通信。保留这种并发，正是 RTS/CTS 比单纯载波侦听强的地方。

explain.en: R is an exposed terminal: it can hear Q, but its signal cannot reach P. Hearing the RTS but not the CTS shows it is not near the receiver and can safely send to someone else. Q can hear R's signal too, but Q is the sender right now, not receiving data, so it is unaffected.
explain.zh: R 是暴露终端：它听得到 Q，但它的信号到不了 P。只听到 RTS、没听到 CTS，就说明自己不在接收者附近，可以安全地发给别人。R 的信号 Q 也听得到，但 Q 此刻是发送方，不在接收数据，不受影响。

title.en: Classic Ethernet: one wire, everyone plugs in
title.zh: 经典以太网：一根线，大家挂上去

text.en: Ethernet is the best-known case of the MAC sublayer; the network port on your dorm wall is talking about it. The earliest **classic Ethernet** is exactly the “share one wire” described above: all machines connect through **transceivers** and interface cables to the same shared cable, which is called the ether. Speeds ran from 3 to 10 Mbps, and after standardisation 10 Mbps is what is usually quoted. Later came **switched Ethernet**, with speeds of 100 Mbps, 1 Gbps, 10 Gbps and so on, covered later.
text.zh: 以太网 (Ethernet) 是 MAC 子层最有名的案例，你宿舍墙上的网口说的就是它。最早的**经典以太网** (classic Ethernet) 正是前面说的「共用一条线」：所有机器经**收发器** (transceiver) 和接口线缆，接到同一根共享线缆上，这根线叫 ether（以太）。速率在 3 到 10 Mbps 之间，标准化之后常说的是 10 Mbps。后来出现了**交换式以太网** (switched Ethernet)，速率是 100 Mbps、1 Gbps、10 Gbps 等，后面会讲它。

alt.en: Four hosts each connect through an interface cable and a transceiver to the same shared cable, with a repeater joining two segments in the middle of the cable
alt.zh: 四台主机各经接口线缆和收发器接到同一根共享线缆上，线缆中间用一个中继器连接两段

caption.en: One shared cable, two segments joined by a repeater.
caption.zh: 一根共享线缆，两段由中继器相连。

text.en: Each kind of cable has a maximum length (the slides' example: 100 m per segment). For a longer wire, join several segments, with a **repeater** between segments: it receives the signal, amplifies it, and forwards it in both directions. Note that a repeater only amplifies and does not look at the content, so the segments are still one shared channel: whoever sends, all segments hear it, and collisions are shared too.
text.zh: 每种线缆有最大长度（课件的例子：每段 100 m）。线要更长，就多接几段，段与段之间用**中继器** (repeater)：它接收信号，放大，再向两个方向转发。注意：中继器只放大，不看内容，所以几段线仍然是同一条共享信道：任何站发，所有段都听得到，冲突也是一起的。

summary.en: Maximum segment lengths for different cables (beyond the slides)
summary.zh: 不同线缆的最大段长（超出课件）

text.en: Early thick coax allowed 500 m per segment, thin coax 185 m, and twisted pair 100 m, consistent with the 100 m in the slides' example.
text.zh: 早期的粗同轴线每段 500 m，细同轴线 185 m，双绞线 100 m，与课件例子里的 100 m 一致。

text.en: With one wire shared by everyone, agreements are needed. The agreements are written into the frame format and the MAC protocol. First, the frame.
text.zh: 一根线所有人共用，就需要约定。约定写在帧的格式和 MAC 协议里。先看帧。

text.en: This is the IEEE 802.3 frame, a format modern Ethernet still uses.
text.zh: 这是 IEEE 802.3 的帧，现代以太网仍然在用这个格式。

alt.en: Ethernet frame: preamble 7 bytes, start of frame 1 byte, destination address 6, source address 6, type or length 2, data 0 to 1500, pad 0 to 46, checksum 4
alt.zh: 以太网帧：前导码 7 字节，帧起始 1 字节，目的地址 6，源地址 6，类型或长度 2，数据 0 到 1500，填充 0 到 46，校验和 4

caption.en: From the destination address to the checksum, at least 64 B together.
caption.zh: 从目的地址到校验和，合起来至少 64 B。

rows.en: A string of alternating 1 and 0 bits, to line the receiver's clock up with the sender's
rows.zh: 一串 1 和 0 交替的位，让接收方的时钟和发送方对上

rows.en: A FLAG byte telling the receiver “the real frame begins now”
rows.zh: 一个 FLAG 字节，告诉接收方「下面真正开始了」

rows.en: Who this frame is for (a MAC address, see next page)
rows.zh: 这一帧发给谁（MAC 地址，见下页）

rows.en: The slides say it “decides which process the frame is handed to”; more precisely, it decides which upper-layer protocol, not a process number. When the value is no more than 1500 it is the length of the data; when it is 1536 or more it is the type (for example IP), telling the receiver which upper-layer protocol to hand the data to
rows.zh: 课件写的是「决定把帧交给哪个进程」；更准确地说，是交给哪个上层协议，不是进程号。数值不大于 1500 时，它是数据的长度；大于等于 1536 时，它是类型（例如 IP），告诉接收方把数据交给哪个上层协议

rows.en: What the upper layer hands down, such as an IP packet. 1500 B is Ethernet's MTU, which you will meet again in the next lesson
rows.zh: 上层交下来的内容，比如一个 IP 包。1500 B 就是以太网的 MTU，下一课会再见到它

rows.en: Fills out data that is too short, so the whole frame is not less than 64 B
rows.zh: 数据太短时补齐，让整帧不小于 64 B

rows.en: A 32-bit checksum; the receiver drops the frame on finding an error (the CRC from the previous lesson)
rows.zh: 32 位校验和，接收方发现错就丢（上一课讲过的 CRC）

text.en: **Minimum frame 64 B** = 6 + 6 + 2 + 46 + 4. That is, data plus pad is at least 46 B: if the data is under 46 B, pad it up to 46 B. The preamble and start of frame only handle synchronisation and are not counted.
text.zh: **最小帧 64 B** = 6 + 6 + 2 + 46 + 4。也就是数据加填充至少 46 B：数据不足 46 B，就用填充补到 46 B。前导码和帧起始只负责同步，不计入。

text.en: Padding is bytes sent for nothing, yet it is not fixed arbitrarily. Why a minimum frame length is needed at all has a page of its own later.
text.zh: 填充是白白多发的字节，却不是随便定的。为什么非要最小帧长，后面有一页专门讲。

prompt.en: In an Ethernet frame, the data is only 20 B. How many bytes of pad are needed for the whole frame (from the destination address to the checksum, not counting the preamble and start of frame) to reach the minimum 64 B?
prompt.zh: 一个以太网帧里，数据只有 20 B。要补多少字节的填充，整个帧（从目的地址到校验和，不计前导码和帧起始）才够最小的 64 B？

hints.en: First add up the mandatory fields: two addresses at 6 B each, type or length 2 B, checksum 4 B. Subtract them from 64 B, and what remains is the least length that data plus pad must have.
hints.zh: 先把必有的字段加起来：两个地址各 6 B，类型或长度 2 B，校验和 4 B。64 B 减去它们，剩下的就是数据加填充至少要有的长度。

explain.en: The mandatory fields are 6+6+2+4=18 B, leaving 64−18=46 B for data plus pad. With 20 B of data, pad 46−20=26 B, and the whole frame is exactly 64 B. If the data were 100 B, no pad would be needed at all.
explain.zh: 必有的字段是 6+6+2+4=18 B，64−18=46 B 留给数据加填充。数据 20 B，补 46−20=26 B，整帧正好 64 B。要是数据有 100 B，就一个填充也不用补。

title.en: MAC address: a network card's factory number
title.zh: MAC 地址：网卡的出厂编号

text.en: The destination and source addresses in the frame are **MAC addresses**: the unique identifier of one physical network card. 48 bits, written as 6 groups of hexadecimal, for example `00:02:2D:66:7C:2C`. Your laptop's network card had one from the factory.
text.zh: 帧里的目的地址和源地址是 **MAC 地址**：一块物理网卡的唯一标识。48 位，写成 6 组十六进制，例如 `00:02:2D:66:7C:2C`。你的笔记本网卡出厂时就有一个。

text.en: Each hexadecimal digit stands for 4 binary bits (0 to F for 0000 to 1111), so each group of two hex digits is exactly 1 byte. Converting group by group to binary:
text.zh: 十六进制每一位对应 4 个二进制位（0 到 F 对应 0000 到 1111），所以每组两位十六进制正好是 1 字节。逐组换成二进制：

text.en: Of the 48 bits, the **first 24 bits** belong to the vendor (the vendor bought a range of numbers) and the **last 24 bits** are the number the vendor gave this card, so there are no repeats anywhere in the world. The all-1s address `FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF` is the **broadcast address**: every station on the LAN receives it.
text.zh: 48 位里，**前 24 位**属于厂商（厂商买下了一段编号），**后 24 位**是厂商给这块网卡编的号，所以全世界不会重复。全是 1 的地址 `FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF` 是**广播地址**：局域网上所有站都收。

text.en: How MAC addresses differ from IP addresses
text.zh: MAC 地址和 IP 地址有什么不同

rows.en: Fixed at the factory by the card
Flat: vendor plus number, with no sign of where it is
rows.zh: 平的：厂商加编号，看不出在哪

rows.en: Hierarchical: a network part plus a host part, showing which network it is in
rows.zh: 有层次：网络部分加主机部分，看得出在哪个网络

rows.en: Across networks, all the way to the destination
rows.zh: 跨网络，一路送到目的地

body.en: Flat numbers are enough within one LAN, but a router cannot possibly remember every network card in the world. Going across networks relies on hierarchical IP addresses (lesson 9). The next lesson will also show that as a packet travels from your laptop to www.unimelb.edu.au, at every router the MAC addresses in the frame are replaced while the IP addresses stay the same.
body.zh: 平的编号在一个局域网里够用，但路由器不可能记住全世界每一块网卡。跨网络要靠有层次的 IP 地址（第 9 课）。下一课还会看到：包从你的笔记本走到 www.unimelb.edu.au，每过一个路由器，帧里的 MAC 地址都要换，IP 地址不变。

title.en: Can MAC addresses alone do the job
title.zh: 能不能只靠 MAC 地址

prompt.en: Someone suggests: let routers simply record where every network card in the world is by MAC address, and then IP addresses would not be needed. Why does this not work?
prompt.zh: 有人提议：路由器干脆记下全世界每一块网卡的 MAC 地址在哪里，这样就不需要 IP 地址了。为什么行不通？

label.en: A MAC address is only 48 bits, too short to hold every network card in the world.
label.zh: MAC 地址只有 48 位，太短，装不下全世界的网卡。

feedback.en: 48 bits can make $2^{48}\approx2.8\times10^{14}$ addresses, which is plenty. The reason they cannot be remembered is not that the numbers are too short, but that you cannot tell from the number where the card is.
feedback.zh: 48 位能编出 $2^{48}\approx2.8\times10^{14}$ 个地址，足够用。记不下的原因不是编号太短，而是编号里看不出网卡在哪。

label.en: Cards from the same vendor share the first 24 bits, so one entry per first-24-bits is enough and IP addresses are not needed.
label.zh: 同一个厂商的网卡，前 24 位相同，所以按前 24 位记一条就行，不需要 IP 地址。

feedback.en: The first 24 bits only say who made it. A vendor's cards are sold all over the world, and which network one is plugged into cannot be seen from the number at all.
feedback.zh: 前 24 位只说明谁生产的。同一个厂商的网卡卖到世界各地，插在哪个网络里，编号完全看不出来。

label.en: A MAC address is flat: the first 24 bits are just the vendor and the last 24 are the vendor's serial number, so you cannot tell which network the card is in. A router could only keep one entry per card, which cannot be held; an IP address begins with a network part, and one entry can cover a whole region.
label.zh: MAC 地址是平的：前 24 位只是厂商，后 24 位是厂商的流水号，看不出网卡在哪个网络。路由器只能一块网卡记一条，记不下；IP 地址前一段是网络部分，一条记录就能管一整片。

label.en: A MAC address is reassigned at every boot, so it cannot be recorded.
label.zh: MAC 地址每次开机都重新分配，所以没法记。

feedback.en: A MAC address is a number fixed at the factory and does not change on boot. What changes with location and is assigned by network is the IP address.
feedback.zh: MAC 地址是网卡出厂时就定下的编号，不会因为开机而变。会随位置变、按网络分配的是 IP 地址。

explain.en: A MAC address is a flat factory number: from the number you cannot see which network the card is in, so a router could only keep one entry per card, and with billions of cards in the world that cannot be held. An IP address is hierarchical, its first part being the network part, so the router only needs to remember “to reach this network, go this way”, and one entry covers a large region. So MAC handles “who in the same LAN to hand the frame to”, and IP handles “which network to deliver to” across networks.
explain.zh: MAC 地址是平的出厂编号：从编号里看不出网卡在哪个网络，路由器只好一块网卡记一条，全世界几十亿块，记不下。IP 地址有层次，前一段是网络部分，路由器只要记「去这个网络往哪走」，一条管一大片。所以 MAC 管的是同一个局域网里「把帧交给谁」，IP 管的是跨网络「送到哪个网络」。

title.en: How Ethernet grabs the line: CSMA/CD and backoff
title.zh: 以太网怎样抢线：CSMA/CD 与退避

text.en: Ethernet's MAC protocol is **1-persistent CSMA/CD**, the ideas above put together:
text.zh: 以太网的 MAC 协议是 **1-持续 CSMA/CD**，就是前面几个想法拼起来：

items.en: Listen first. If the line is busy, keep listening, and send the moment it goes idle (1-persistent).
items.zh: 先听。线忙就一直听着，一空闲马上发（1-持续）。

items.en: Listen while sending. If what you hear differs from what you sent, there was a collision.
items.zh: 边发边听。听到的和自己发的不一样，就是撞了。

items.en: As soon as you find a collision, stop sending at once, and send a short jam signal so that all stations know there was a collision.
items.zh: 一发现冲突，立刻停发，再发一小段干扰信号，让所有站都知道撞了。

items.en: Wait a random while and try again. How long to wait is worked out by binary exponential backoff.
items.zh: 随机等一会儿再来。等多久，由二进制指数退避算出。

text.en: Binary exponential backoff (BEB)
text.zh: 二进制指数退避 (binary exponential backoff, BEB)

text.en: If this frame has already collided $i$ times, pick a random integer from $0$ to $2^i-1$ and wait that many **slots** before trying again. A slot is the transmission time of 512 bits: at 10 Mbps that is 51.2 microseconds (where it comes from, the next page will show).
text.zh: 这一帧已经撞了 $i$ 次，就在 $0$ 到 $2^i-1$ 里随机挑一个整数，等那么多个**时隙** (slot) 再重新来。时隙是 512 位的发送时间：10 Mbps 时是 51.2 微秒（它从哪来，下一页会看到）。

head.en: How many times this frame has collided, i

text.en: After two stations have both collided $i$ times, each picks at random from $2^i$ numbers, and the probability they pick the same is $1/2^i$: the more they have collided, the less likely they are to collide again.
text.zh: 两个站同时撞过 $i$ 次之后，各自从 $2^i$ 个数里随机挑，挑得一样的概率是 $1/2^i$：撞得越多，越不容易再撞。

text.en: Why not fix one range? Because a station does not know how many stations are contending right now. If the range is too small, with many stations it keeps colliding; if too large, with few stations it waits for nothing. Doubling the range at each collision amounts to estimating “roughly how many stations” as it collides: with few stations it is settled quickly, with many it spreads out automatically.
text.zh: 为什么不固定在一个范围？因为站不知道现在有几个站在抢。范围太小，站多时一直撞；范围太大，站少时白白等。每撞一次范围翻倍，等于一边撞一边估计「大概有多少站」：站少时很快解决，站多时自动拉开。

body.en: The standard allows at most 16 tries, then gives up and reports an error; after $i$ passes 10, the range stops growing and stays at 0 to 1023.
body.zh: 标准里最多试 16 次，还不成功就放弃并报错；$i$ 超过 10 以后，范围不再增大，停在 0 到 1023。

prompt.en: Two stations send a frame at the same time and collide; on the resend they collide again; on the next resend they collide again: this frame has now collided 3 times. Now both stations follow binary exponential backoff, each picking a random integer and waiting that many slots before trying again. In what range does each station pick? What is the probability the two stations pick the same number this time and collide once more?
prompt.zh: 两个站同时发了一帧，撞了；重发时又撞了；再重发又撞了：这一帧已经撞了 3 次。现在两个站都按二进制指数退避，各自随机挑一个整数，等那么多个时隙再试。每个站在哪个范围里挑？两个站这次挑到同一个数、再撞一次的概率是多少？

label.en: 0 to 3, probability 1/4

feedback.en: This is the range after 2 collisions ($2^2-1=3$). This frame has collided 3 times, $i=3$, so the range is 0 to $2^3-1=7$.

label.en: 0 to 7, probability 1/7

feedback.en: The range is right, but 0 to 7 is 8 numbers in all, not 7. Each of the two stations picks from 8 numbers, and the probability of picking the same one is 1/8.
feedback.zh: 范围对，但 0 到 7 一共是 8 个数，不是 7 个。两个站各从 8 个数里挑，挑到同一个的概率是 1/8。

label.en: 0 to 7, probability 1/8
0 to 15, probability 1/16

feedback.en: This is the range after 4 collisions ($2^4-1=15$). After 3 collisions it is 0 to 7.
feedback.zh: 这是撞了 4 次时的范围（$2^4-1=15$）。撞了 3 次就是 0 到 7。

hints.en: After $i$ collisions the range is 0 to $2^i-1$. What is $i$ here? How many numbers are in that range?
hints.zh: 撞了 $i$ 次，范围是 0 到 $2^i-1$。这里 $i$ 是多少？这个范围里一共有几个数？

explain.en: After $i$ collisions, pick from 0 to $2^i-1$: for $i=3$ that is 0 to 7, 8 numbers. Each of the two stations picks one, and the probability of picking the same is $1/8$. If they collide once more, the range doubles to 0 to 15, and the probability of colliding again is halved, to $1/16$.
explain.zh: 撞过 $i$ 次，在 0 到 $2^i-1$ 里挑：$i=3$ 时是 0 到 7，共 8 个数。两个站各挑一个，挑到同一个的概率是 $1/8$。再撞一次，范围翻倍成 0 到 15，再撞的概率就减半，成 $1/16$。

title.en: Why a frame cannot be too short

text.en: Ethernet finds collisions by “listening while sending”. But for A to hear a collision, it must **still be sending** when the noise from the collision comes back. Say the signal takes $\tau$ to go from A to B (the longer the wire, the larger $\tau$). The worst case goes like this:
text.zh: 以太网靠「边发边听」发现冲突。可是 A 要听到冲突，必须在撞出的噪声回来的时候**还在发送**。设信号从 A 传到 B 要 $\tau$（线越长，$\tau$ 越大）。最坏的情形是这样：

alt.en: Space-time diagram: A starts sending at time 0; B starts sending just before τ, and the collision happens at B at time τ; the noise returns to A at time 2τ, and A must keep sending until then
alt.zh: 时空图：A 在时刻 0 开始发；B 在 τ 之前一点才开始发，在时刻 τ 于 B 处冲突；噪声在时刻 2τ 回到 A，A 必须一直发到那时

caption.en: Horizontal is distance, vertical is time. The blue line is A's frame, and the red dashed line is the collision noise.
caption.zh: 横向是距离，纵向是时间。蓝线是 A 的帧，红虚线是冲突的噪声。

items.zh: A 在时刻 0 开始发。

items.en: B listens at $\tau-\varepsilon$: A's frame is just short of arriving, the line still looks idle, so B starts sending too.
items.zh: B 在 $\tau-\varepsilon$ 去听：A 的帧还差一点才到，线上看起来还是空闲，所以 B 也开始发。

items.en: At time $\tau$, the two frames collide at B.
items.zh: 时刻 $\tau$，两个帧在 B 处撞上。

items.en: The noise has to travel another $\tau$ back to A, arriving at time $2\tau$.
items.zh: 噪声再传回 A，还要走 $\tau$，到达时刻是 $2\tau$。

text.en: So A must send for at least $2\tau$. If A finishes before $2\tau$, it will think it succeeded, when the frame was in fact ruined long ago. If B starts sending earlier, the collision is earlier and the noise comes back earlier, so $2\tau$ is the worst case.
text.zh: 所以 A 必须至少发到 $2\tau$。如果 A 在 $2\tau$ 之前就发完了，它会以为成功，其实帧早已被撞坏。B 如果更早开始发，冲突就更早，噪声回来得也更早，所以 $2\tau$ 是最坏的情形。

text.en: The time to send a frame equals frame length divided by bandwidth. For 10 Mbps Ethernet, the standard fixes the worst-case round-trip time at $2\tau = 51.2\ \mu\text{s}$ (already leaving margin for the delays of repeaters and so on). So the minimum frame length is:
text.zh: 发一帧的时间等于帧长除以带宽。10 Mbps 的以太网，标准把最坏的往返时间定为 $2\tau = 51.2\ \mu\text{s}$（已经为中继器等的延迟留够余量）。于是最小帧长是：

text.en: Exactly $6+6+2+46+4=64$ B. Now it all connects: the job of the **pad** is to make even a frame with very little data last the full $2\tau$. 51.2 microseconds is also exactly the length of one slot in backoff.
text.zh: 正好是 $6+6+2+46+4=64$ B。这就连起来了：**填充 (pad)** 的作用，是让数据再短的帧也发满 $2\tau$。51.2 微秒也正是退避里一个时隙的长度。

prompt.en: Imagine a shared wire whose bandwidth rises to 100 Mbps, with the frame format unchanged and the minimum frame still 64 B (512 bits). To still find collisions by “listening while sending”, what is the largest worst-case round-trip time $2\tau$ of the whole network, in microseconds?
prompt.zh: 想象一条共享线，带宽升到 100 Mbps，帧格式不变，最小帧仍是 64 B（512 位）。为了还能靠「边发边听」发现冲突，整个网络最坏的往返时间 $2\tau$ 最多是多少微秒？

hints.en: The minimum frame has to last $2\tau$: time to send a frame = frame length ÷ bandwidth.
hints.zh: 最小帧要发满 $2\tau$：发一帧的时间 = 帧长 ÷ 带宽。

explain.en: 512 bits ÷ 100 Mbps = 5.12 microseconds, only a tenth of the value at 10 Mbps. The cable length also has to shrink to about a tenth, or the minimum frame will have finished sending before the collision noise comes back. So as speeds go up, the shared wire no longer works, and Ethernet turns to switches.
explain.zh: 512 位 ÷ 100 Mbps = 5.12 微秒，只有 10 Mbps 时的十分之一。线缆长度也得缩到大约十分之一，否则最小帧发完了冲突的噪声还没回来。所以速度往上走时，共享线行不通了，以太网转向交换机。

intro.en: First the symbols: $F$ is the frame length (bits), $B$ is the bandwidth (bits per second), $L$ is the cable length (metres), $c$ is the speed of the signal in the cable (metres per second, about $2\times10^{8}$), and $e\approx 2.718$ is the constant that appeared earlier. Efficiency means: of the channel's time, what fraction goes to carrying useful frames.
intro.zh: 先说清符号：$F$ 是帧长（位），$B$ 是带宽（位/秒），$L$ 是线缆长度（米），$c$ 是信号在线里的传播速度（米/秒，约 $2\times10^{8}$），$e\approx 2.718$ 是前面出现过的常数。效率的意思是：信道的时间里，有多大比例在送有用的帧。

why.en: The time to send a frame: number of bits divided by bits per second.
why.zh: 发一帧要的时间：位数除以每秒位数。

why.en: One contention (one slot) takes at most one round trip, that is, $2\tau$.
why.zh: 一次竞争（一个时隙）最长是一个往返，也就是 $2\tau$。

why.en: In the ideal case, each slot succeeds with probability $1/e$, so on average $e$ slots are tried before getting the line, and every frame sent pays on average $e$ slots of contention time.
why.zh: 最理想时，每个时隙成功的概率是 $1/e$，平均要试 $e$ 个时隙才抢到线，所以每发一帧平均要付 $e$ 个时隙的竞争时间。

why.en: The fraction of the total time that is useful.
why.zh: 有用的时间占全部时间的比例。

why.en: Multiply numerator and denominator by $B/F$ and you get the form in the slides.
why.zh: 分子分母同乘 $B/F$，就是课件里的写法。

outro.en: Take $B=10$ Mbps, $L=2500$ m (the largest span of a whole 10 Mbps Ethernet network), $c=2\times10^{8}$ m/s: $2\tau=2L/c=25$ microseconds, and one contention takes on average $e\cdot2\tau\approx68$ microseconds. For a minimum frame of 512 bits: sending takes 51.2 microseconds, and efficiency is about $51.2/(51.2+68)\approx43\%$. A full-length frame is about 12000 bits: sending takes 1200 microseconds, and efficiency is about $1200/(1200+68)\approx95\%$. Reading the formula: when $B$ or $L$ grows, $2BLe/(cF)$ grows and efficiency falls; the longer $F$ is, the higher the efficiency. Intuition: the larger the bandwidth, the faster the same frame is sent, while contention time depends only on distance and does not shrink, so the fraction contention takes rises. (The 51.2 microseconds on the minimum-frame page is the worst-case round trip with the margin the standard leaves; here we count only the cable's own propagation, hence 25 microseconds.)
outro.zh: 取 $B=10$ Mbps，$L=2500$ m（10 Mbps 以太网整个网络的最大跨度），$c=2\times10^{8}$ m/s：$2\tau=2L/c=25$ 微秒，竞争一次平均 $e\cdot2\tau\approx68$ 微秒。最小帧 512 位：发 51.2 微秒，效率约 $51.2/(51.2+68)\approx43\%$。满长的帧约 12000 位：发 1200 微秒，效率约 $1200/(1200+68)\approx95\%$。读公式：$B$ 或 $L$ 变大，$2BLe/(cF)$ 变大，效率变低；$F$ 越长，效率越高。直觉：带宽越大，同样一帧发得越快，而竞争的时间只由距离决定，不会缩短，竞争占的比例就上升。（最小帧那页的 51.2 微秒是标准留足余量后的最坏往返；这里只算线缆本身的传播，所以是 25 微秒。）

prompt.en: The same cable ($L=2500$ m, $c=2\times10^{8}$ m/s), with bandwidth raised to $B=100$ Mbps, frame length $F=12000$ bits, $e\approx2.718$. About what is the channel efficiency? (Enter a percentage)
prompt.zh: 同样的线缆（$L=2500$ m，$c=2\times10^{8}$ m/s），带宽升到 $B=100$ Mbps，帧长 $F=12000$ 位，$e\approx2.718$。信道效率约是多少？（填百分数）

explain.en: The values of $B$ and $c$ both have a factor of $10^8$, which cancels: $2BLe/(cF)=2500\times2.718/12000\approx0.566$, and efficiency is $1/1.566\approx63.8\%$. With the same cable and frame, at 10 Mbps it was about 95%, and now it drops to about 64%: bandwidth ×10, and the fraction taken by contention goes up. To bring efficiency back, either shrink the cable to a tenth or lengthen the frame.
explain.zh: $B$ 和 $c$ 的数值里都有 $10^8$ 的因子，可以约掉：$2BLe/(cF)=2500\times2.718/12000\approx0.566$，效率 $1/1.566\approx63.8\%$。同样的线和帧，10 Mbps 时约 95%，现在掉到约 64%：带宽 ×10，竞争占的比例就上来了。要把效率拉回去，要么把线缩到十分之一，要么把帧加长。

title.en: Hubs and switches: no more fighting for the line
title.zh: 集线器与交换机：不再抢线

text.en: The trouble with classic Ethernet: all stations are in one **collision domain**, and any two stations sending at once collide. The more stations, the more collisions, and as the last page showed, the greater the bandwidth, the worse the loss from collisions.
text.zh: 经典以太网的毛病：所有站在同一个**冲突域** (collision domain) 里，任意两个站同时发就撞。站越多越撞，而上一页算过，带宽越大撞得越亏。

alt.zh: 左：集线器把四个站的线汇到一个点；右：交换机把站两两接通，两对站同时通信互不干扰

caption.en: A hub is one collision domain; in a switch each port is its own collision domain.
caption.zh: 集线器是一个冲突域；交换机里每个端口各是一个冲突域。

text.en: A **hub** is like a multi-port repeater: a signal received on one port goes out unchanged from all the other ports. All devices on a hub are still in the same collision domain, still need CSMA/CD, and the total throughput is the speed of that one wire.
text.zh: **集线器** (hub) 像多口的中继器：一个口收到信号，原样从其他所有口发出去。接在集线器上的所有设备还是在同一个冲突域里，还要 CSMA/CD，总吞吐量就是那一条线的速度。

text.en: A **switch** looks at the destination MAC address in the frame and sends the frame only to the port where the destination station is. Each port is its own collision domain. Different pairs of ports can communicate at the same time: while one pair of stations communicates, another pair is communicating too, and total throughput is much greater than a hub's.
text.zh: **交换机** (switch) 看帧里的目的 MAC 地址，只把帧送到目的站所在的端口。每个端口自己是一个冲突域。不同的端口对可以同时通信：一对站通信的同时，另一对也在通信，总吞吐量比集线器大得多。

text.en: Modern network cable is **full-duplex**: sending and receiving each have their own wires, and the two directions do not affect each other at the same moment. Each port on a switch connects just one device, so this wire has only two ends, “device” and “switch”, each in charge of its own direction, and nobody competes with it for the same direction. So full-duplex lines no longer need CSMA/CD.
text.zh: 现代的网线是**全双工** (full-duplex)：收和发各走各的线，同一时刻两个方向互不影响。交换机的每个端口只接一台设备，这条线上只有「设备」和「交换机」两端，各管各的方向，没有人和它抢同一个方向。所以全双工线路上不再需要 CSMA/CD。

text.en: With no need to find collisions by CSMA/CD, the limit that “the wire cannot be too long”, set originally for finding collisions, disappears with it (cable length is left with only signal quality as a limit). The frame format is kept unchanged, including the minimum of 64 B, for compatibility with old equipment. Ethernet has therefore climbed to 100 Mbps, 1 Gbps and 10 Gbps. The network port on your dorm wall usually connects to a switch.
text.zh: 不用靠 CSMA/CD 发现冲突，当初为发现冲突而定的「线不能太长」这条限制，也就跟着没了（线长只剩信号质量的限制）。帧的格式却原样保留，包括最小 64 B，为的是和老设备兼容。以太网因此一路升到 100 Mbps、1 Gbps、10 Gbps。你宿舍墙上的网口，连的通常就是一台交换机。

summary.en: How a switch knows which port to send to (beyond the slides)
summary.zh: 交换机怎么知道往哪个口送（超出课件）

text.en: A switch looks at the **source** MAC address of every frame it receives and notes “this address is on this port”, storing it in a forwarding table. After that, a frame sent to a known address goes out only from the matching port; if the address is not yet known, or it is the broadcast address (all 1s), it goes out of all the other ports. After a few exchanges the table is complete, with nobody having to configure it.
text.zh: 交换机看每个收到的帧的**源** MAC 地址，记下「这个地址在这个端口」，存成转发表 (forwarding table)。之后收到发往已知地址的帧，只从对应端口送出；地址还不认识，或是广播地址（全 1），就从其他所有端口发出去。通信几次，表就记全了，不用人去配置。

title.en: Don't think there is still fighting for the line on a switch
title.zh: 别以为交换机上还在抢线

body.en: On a full-duplex line each port has only one device, and nobody competes with it for the same direction, so there is no need for CSMA/CD and no collisions occur.
body.zh: 全双工线路上每个端口只有一台设备，没有谁和它争同一个方向，所以不需要 CSMA/CD，也不会发生冲突。

title.en: The same wire, a different device

prompt.en: Four computers A, B, C, D are all connected by 100 Mbps wires to the same device. A wants to send to B, and C wants to send to D; both paths want to fill the line speed and start at the same time. (1) If the device is a hub, what is the most the two paths can carry together? What if it is a switch? (2) Why is CSMA/CD no longer needed on a switch port?
prompt.zh: 四台电脑 A、B、C、D 都用 100 Mbps 的线接到同一台设备上。A 要发给 B，C 要发给 D，两路都想用满线速，同时开始。(1) 这台设备如果是集线器，两路加起来最多能送多少？如果是交换机呢？(2) 为什么交换机的一个端口上，不再需要 CSMA/CD？

key_points.en: Hub: all devices are in one collision domain, only one path can carry at a time, and the two together carry at most about 100 Mbps (and they have to fight for the line and will collide)
key_points.zh: 集线器：所有设备在同一个冲突域，同一时刻只有一路能送，两路加起来最多约 100 Mbps（还要抢线、会撞）

key_points.en: Switch: each port is its own collision domain, A→B and C→D do not interfere and can communicate at the same time, together carrying at most about 200 Mbps
key_points.zh: 交换机：每个端口各是一个冲突域，A→B 和 C→D 互不干扰，可以同时通信，加起来最多约 200 Mbps

key_points.en: On a full-duplex line sending and receiving use separate wires, each port connects only one device, and nobody competes with it for the same direction, so there is no collision and no need for CSMA/CD
key_points.zh: 全双工线路上收和发各走各的线，每个端口只接一台设备，没有谁和它抢同一个方向，所以不会冲突，不需要 CSMA/CD

model_answer.en: A hub puts all devices in one collision domain; while A→B holds the line, C→D can only wait (or collide), and the two together carry at most the 100 Mbps of one wire. A switch looks at the destination MAC address and sends the frame only to the destination port; each port is its own collision domain, A→B and C→D use different pairs of ports and both run at full speed at the same time, together about 200 Mbps. CSMA/CD is not needed on a switch port because a full-duplex line has separate wires for sending and receiving, and there is only one device at the other end of the port, so nobody competes with it for the same direction and there are no collisions.
model_answer.zh: 集线器把所有设备放进同一个冲突域，A→B 占着线时 C→D 只能等（或者撞），两路加起来最多只有一条线的 100 Mbps。交换机看目的 MAC 地址，只把帧送到目的端口，每个端口是自己的冲突域，A→B 和 C→D 走不同的端口对，同时跑满，加起来约 200 Mbps。交换机端口上不需要 CSMA/CD，是因为全双工线路收发各走一条线，端口另一头只有一台设备，没有谁和它争同一个方向，不会冲突。

hints.en: Think: how many collision domains do all the devices on a hub form? And on a switch? On one full-duplex wire, how many devices compete for the same direction?
hints.zh: 想一想：集线器接上的所有设备是几个冲突域？交换机呢？一条全双工的线上，有几个设备在争同一个方向？

explain.en: All devices on a hub are in one collision domain; while one path holds the line the other must wait, and together they carry at most the speed of one wire. A switch isolates each port into its own collision domain, two pairs of stations use different ports and do not interfere, and both can run at full speed at once. CSMA/CD is not needed on a port because a full-duplex line has separate wires for sending and receiving, and there is only one device at the other end, so nobody competes with it for the same direction.
explain.zh: 集线器的所有设备在同一个冲突域，一路占着线，另一路就得等，合起来最多一条线的速度。交换机把每个端口隔成各自的冲突域，两对站走不同的端口，互不影响，能同时跑满。端口上用不着 CSMA/CD，是因为全双工线路收发各走一条线，另一头又只有一台设备，没有谁和它争同一个方向。

text.en: Compare this lesson's methods in one table:
text.zh: 把这一课的办法放在同一张表里比一比：

rows.en: Listen before sending; CD listens while sending and stops at a collision
rows.zh: 先听再发；CD 边发边听，一撞就停

rows.en: Many collisions; CD makes the loss from ruined frames smaller
rows.zh: 冲突多，CD 让撞坏的损失变小

rows.en: Register or compare addresses first, then send in turn
rows.zh: 先登记或比地址，再轮流发

rows.en: Must wait a round, or the overhead is a large fraction
rows.zh: 要等一轮，或开销占比大

rows.en: Shared wires with permanently high load
rows.zh: 负载一直很高的共享线
自适应树遍历（受限竞争）

rows.en: On a collision, split in half and keep splitting only within the colliding group
rows.zh: 冲突就对半分，只在冲突的组里继续分

rows.en: Starts at the root, hardly any waste
Starts at a deep level, close to taking turns
Wanting to serve both ends of the load
RTS/CTS first, and stations that hear them defer
One extra round of short frames
Control frames are very short, cheaper than ruining data frames
rows.zh: 控制帧很短，比撞坏数据帧划算

rows.en: Wireless LANs: hidden and exposed terminals
rows.zh: 无线局域网：隐藏终端与暴露终端

rows.en: Each port has a full-duplex wire to itself, no fighting for the line
rows.zh: 每个端口独占一条全双工线，不抢线

rows.en: Different pairs of ports communicate at the same time, large total throughput
rows.zh: 不同端口对同时通信，总吞吐量大

text.en: Back to that one click: the frame your laptop sends goes over Wi-Fi in the dorm (wireless, which has to deal with hidden terminals), or over a network cable to a switch (wired, full-duplex, no more fighting for the line). This frame is only responsible for getting to the next device: the router. How it goes on from the router is for the next lesson.
text.zh: 回到那一次点击：你的笔记本发出的帧，在宿舍里走 Wi-Fi（无线，要对付隐藏终端），或者走网线接到交换机（有线，全双工，不再抢线）。这一帧只负责走到下一台设备：路由器。路由器再往下怎么走，是下一课的事。

prompt.en: Three scenarios: (1) late at night, a shared wire where only two computers occasionally send data; (2) the night before a big exam, a shared wire where 40 computers always have data to send; (3) Wi-Fi in a reading room, where some users cannot hear each other across the bookshelves yet are all connected to the same access point. Which group gives the most suitable approach for each?
prompt.zh: 三个场景：(1) 深夜，只有两台电脑偶尔发数据的共享线；(2) 大考前夜，40 台电脑一直都有数据要发的共享线；(3) 阅览室里的 Wi-Fi，有些用户彼此隔着书架听不到对方，却都连着同一个接入点。各自最合适的思路是哪一组？

label.en: (1) bit map, (2) ALOHA, (3) carrier sensing alone is enough
label.zh: (1) 位图，(2) ALOHA，(3) 只靠载波侦听就够

feedback.en: This is the wrong way round: a bit map at low load waits a whole round for nothing, ALOHA at high load collides most fiercely; and the users in (3) who cannot hear each other are exactly where carrier sensing fails.
feedback.zh: 这是反过来了：位图在低负载时要白等一整轮，ALOHA 在高负载时撞得最凶；而 (3) 里彼此听不到的用户正是载波侦听失灵的地方。

label.en: (1) contention (send when you want, CSMA/CD), (2) collision-free or limited contention (taking turns, groups), (3) a MACA such as RTS/CTS
label.zh: (1) 竞争（想发就发、CSMA/CD），(2) 无冲突或受限竞争（轮流、分组），(3) RTS/CTS 一类的 MACA

label.en: (1) collision-free, (2) contention, (3) carrier sensing alone is enough
label.zh: (1) 无冲突，(2) 竞争，(3) 只靠载波侦听就够

feedback.en: (1) At low load collision-free waits for nothing and contention is better; (2) at high load contention collides without end; (3) users who cannot hear each other across the shelves are hidden terminals, and carrier sensing alone will collide.
feedback.zh: (1) 低负载时无冲突要白等，竞争更好；(2) 高负载时竞争撞个不停；(3) 隔着书架听不到对方的用户是隐藏终端，只靠载波侦听会撞。

label.en: Use Ethernet's CSMA/CD for all three
label.zh: 三个场景都用以太网的 CSMA/CD

feedback.en: CSMA/CD finds collisions by listening while sending, which requires the signal to reach the whole wire, and it cannot solve hidden terminals in wireless. At high load its efficiency is also far below taking turns.
feedback.zh: CSMA/CD 靠边发边听发现冲突，要求信号能传遍整条线，而且不能解决无线里的隐藏终端。高负载时它的效率也远不如轮流。

explain.en: At low load use contention, because you send when you want and hardly wait; at high load use collision-free or limited contention, because taking turns does not waste time on collisions; hidden terminals in wireless need MACA's RTS/CTS, so that the area around the receiver learns first that someone wants to send.
explain.zh: 低负载用竞争，因为想发就发、几乎不用等；高负载用无冲突或受限竞争，因为轮流发不会白白撞掉时间；无线里的隐藏终端要靠 MACA 的 RTS/CTS，让接收者所在的一带先知道有人要发。
